newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico revised November trade surplus $254 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico revised November trade surplus $254 mln.

text.p: Mexico's revised trade surplus for November 1996 was $254 million, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
The surplus was based on exports of $8,472 million, the second-highest month on record and a 22.5 percent increase over November 1995, and imports of $8,218 million, the ministry said.

The government's initial estimate of the trade surplus for November, released on December 22, was $280 million, but was revised largely because of revised figures for automobile imports and exports, the ministry said. Regardless, it was Mexico's 22nd consecutive month of trade surpluses.

Exports of non-petroleum products totalled $7.464 billion in November, a growth of 18.4 percent over the same month a year earlier. Petroleum exports of $1.008 billion represented a 67 percent increase over November 1995.

Of the total of $8.218 billion in imports, 79.1 percent was represented by intermediate goods and 12.6 percent by capital goods. Industry bought 91.7 percent of the imports while consumers accounted for the remaining 8.3 percent.
Mexico's accumulated trade surplus for the first 11 months of 1996 totalled $6.072 billion based on exports of $87.499 billion and imports of $81.427 billion.
